slides.title: 12.1.1 Maintaining Heap Properties
keyPoints: In a zero-based array, the children of index p are 2p+1 and 2p+2 when those indices exist.
The parent of a nonroot index i is (i-1)/2.
In a minimum heap, every parent is no greater than either child.
This makes the root a minimum of the entire heap because every downward path is nondecreasing.
slides.narration: In Book III, Chapter 12, treat 12.1.1 Maintaining Heap Properties as an algorithmic claim. In a zero-based array, the children of index p are 2p+1 and 2p+2 when those indices exist. The complete-tree shape gives logarithmic height independently of the values and their arrival order; there is no pointer-tree degeneration from inserting sorted keys. slides.title: 12.2.1 Inserting Prioritized Values
keyPoints: Insertion appends the new value at the next complete-tree position.
Every old parent-child relationship remains valid except possibly the new value’s relationship with its parent.
Sift upward while the child is smaller, exchanging with its parent until the rule holds or the root is reached.
Each exchange moves up one level, giving O(log n) comparisons in the worst case.

slides.title: Failure clinic — The smaller sibling stayed below a larger parent
keyPoints: After removing the minimum, the next result is wrong even though the root was swapped with one child.
Inspect child selection in sift-down.
Choosing the first available child instead of the smaller child can leave the other child violating order.
A heap works for odd sizes but reads beyond the end for an even size.
slides.narration: In Book III, Chapter 12, treat Failure clinic — The smaller sibling stayed below a larger parent as an algorithmic claim. After removing the minimum, the next result is wrong even though the root was swapped with one child. Inspect child selection in sift-down. Choosing the first available child instead of the smaller child can leave the other child violating order immediately. A heap works for odd sizes but reads beyond the end for an even size. The final internal node may have only a left child. Check the right-child existence condition separately from the left-child guarantee. A three-element fixture cannot expose every incomplete-final-level case. An unsigned construction loop hangs after processing the root. Replace a >= 0 countdown with a positive counter and a derived i-1 index. The wraparound is a type-domain defect, not evidence that heap construction is inherently difficult to terminate. At a graduate level, the answer is never just that the code ran. Ask what invariant is preserved, what state changes, why termination follows, what input size controls cost, and what output or diagnostic proves the implementation matched the specification.
